claims.text: Every adapter here exposes the same shape -- ask(prompt, *, role, timeout_s, model=None) -> VendorReply -- over four vendors
claims.why: Adapter classes are not defined in this chunk; cannot verify method signature.

claims.text: VendorReply carries no approve/reject/score/verdict/majority field and must never grow one
claims.why: VendorReply class definition not present in this chunk.

claims.text: status here is a TRANSPORT status (did the bytes make the round trip), not a judgement about the work under review.
claims.why: VendorReply definition not shown; cannot verify status field semantics.

claims.text: The premise -- 'independent vendors have independent blind spots, so cross-vendor disagreement is informative' -- is plausible and UNTESTED here. It is refuted as follows, and the measurement must exist before any council is wired into a real review workflow
claims.why: No measurement code present in this chunk; cannot verify that the falsification protocol is implemented elsewhere.

claims.text: Council profiles are deliberately NOT adapters.subprocess_adapter.RUNTIME_PROFILES: those carry --sandbox workspace-write and --permission-mode dontAsk and spawn in the primary checkout
claims.why: COUNCIL_PROFILES and RUNTIME_PROFILES are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: codex runs exec --sandbox read-only with approvals off; claude runs -p with tools disallowed and NO dontAsk; every subprocess is spawned in a FRESH EMPTY TEMP DIRECTORY that is not the repo, not a worktree and contains no repo files (see council_cwd)
claims.why: Profile definitions and council_cwd() implementation not in this chunk.

claims.text: The secret floor runs PER FILE before any bytes leave the process: the PATH channel over each evidence path individually, the CONTENT channel per file, and a content-only backstop over the assembled prompt. A hit REFUSES the call (status='refused_by_floor'); there is no redact-and-send, and the runner is never invoked.
claims.why: floor_check() and related logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: OLLAMA_HOST is NEVER set, mutated or inherited by anything in this module.
claims.why: Cannot verify absence of OLLAMA_HOST assignment across entire file without seeing all chunks.

claims.text: offload.py:193-197 justifies lane='trusted' (tier-2 egress DISABLED, full repo source inlined, withheld=[]) by the claim 'this is called for the local bench alone (ollama: no bytes leave the machine)'. That claim is a property of an environment variable nobody had ever set.
claims.why: References offload.py which is not in this chunk; no environment variable code shown.

claims.text: the host is passed explicitly per call, and whether it counts as local is decided by sensitivity.lane_for_host -- the ONE implementation of 'do the bytes leave this machine', shared with the gate it switches.
claims.why: lane_for_host imported but not invoked in this chunk; implementation not shown.

claims.text: NUMERIC LOOPBACK ONLY: localhost does NOT count, because a name is a DNS indirection the predicate cannot see through.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements or tests this logic.

claims.text: codex and agy default to lane='untrusted': the allow-list / default-deny tier is ON for them, and withheld paths are named.
claims.why: No default lane assignments shown in this chunk.

claims.text: runtime_registry.py currently marks codex_cli trusted-with-IP and openai_api not -- same company, opposite verdict -- so no default here inherits that.
claims.why: References runtime_registry.py not in this chunk.
